mesh.printCheck.openEdges.comment: Plural key (one count sentence; the first formatter argument chooses the plural form and is never printed, the second is the count already formatted for the locale). Print-check line of a 3D model preview: the number of open edges, meaning edges that only one triangle of the surface uses, so the surface has a gap there and is not watertight. Shown only when the count is above zero. Say it as a fact about the surface; never claim the model is broken or cannot be printed. Count of the displayed tessellation. Draft translations pending native-speaker review.

mesh.printCheck.nonManifoldEdges.comment: Plural key (one count sentence; the first formatter argument chooses the plural form and is never printed, the second is the count already formatted for the locale). Print-check line of a 3D model preview: the number of edges that more than two faces of the surface share. A solid's surface cannot have such an edge, and it makes a slicer's idea of inside and outside ambiguous. Shown only when the count is above zero. Say it as a fact about the surface; never claim the model is broken or cannot be printed. Do not write the number two as a digit. Count of the displayed tessellation. Draft translations pending native-speaker review.

mesh.printCheck.estimate.comment: Formatted key. Estimate line of a 3D model preview, shown only when the model's volume is known and its length unit is declared or assumed to be millimetres. It says what the model would use if it were printed completely solid in PLA, a common 3D-printing plastic, and it must be honest that this is an upper bound because slicing software usually prints with less infill than solid. Argument 1 is the mass already formatted for the locale and argument 2 its localized unit symbol (grams, for example g); argument 3 is the length of filament already formatted and argument 4 its localized unit symbol (metres, for example m); argument 5 is the filament diameter already formatted (1.75) and argument 6 its localized unit symbol (millimetres, for example mm). Keep the six positional placeholders; the order may change where the language needs it, and each unit goes after its number the way the language writes units. Do not add singular or plural forms: word it so it reads naturally for any number. Approximate value computed from the displayed tessellation, not a promise about a print. Draft translations pending native-speaker review.
